root_cause.text: The driver fails to validate that the user-supplied RX ring size (rx_pending) is above a required minimum before passing it to the `Q_SIZE` macro, which performs a bit-shift operation that becomes undefined when given a value below 16 (e.g., zero), triggering a shift-out-of-bounds error.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check `if (ring->rx_pending < 16)` returning `-EINVAL` before the `Q_COUNT(Q_SIZE(rx_count, 3))` call, and the commit message explicitly states it fixes "UBSAN: shift-out-of-bounds error" caused by "small or zero ring sizes via ethtool -G".

bic_trace_step.reason: In the function otx2_set_ringparam() (lines ~273-278 of the added file), the code takes user-supplied rx_pending without validating it is at least 16. It only ensures it is not less than pfvf->hw.rq_skid, but does not enforce the documented minimum of 16. Thus a value below 16 (e.g., 0) is passed to Q_SIZE() macro, which performs a bit-shift that becomes undefined for values < 16.
